messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: Partially-Centered Parameterizations
parts:
Hi, could someone please let me know what is the rstan function that returns treedepth, actual number of leapfrog steps, and average acceptance probabilty for
the slice, for each iteration of a Stan run?
Thanks
A


> On Oct 22, 2015, at 11:27 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
>
> RStan gives you treedepth, actual number of leapfrog steps (which may be less
> than 2^depth due to divergences), and average acceptance probabilty for
> the slice as detailed in Hoffman and Gelman and in the Stan manual.
>
> How do you compute "expected squared jumped distance" from a chain?
>
> I can't remember how to get the info in RStan --- it's documented somewhere
> in the fit object, I think. The values are stored in the fit object in
> some parallel data structure to the draws.
>
> Michael and Andrew should put their heads together to negotiate minimal
> vs. maximal reporting defaults. CmdStan just includes them in the summary
> output and gives them in the CSV file output, but they're not included
> in RStan's print(fit).
>
> - Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Partially-Centered Parameterizations
parts:
sampler_params <- get_sampler_params(fit, inc_warmup=FALSE)
names(sampler_params)

Or to aggregate over the chains as the samples themselves are,

sapply(sampler_params, function(x) c(x[,’sampler_param_name']))[,1]
On Oct 25, 2015, at 4:17 PM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:

Hi, could someone please let me know what is the rstan function that returns treedepth, actual number of leapfrog steps, and average acceptance probabilty for
the slice, for each iteration of a Stan run?
Thanks
A


On Oct 22, 2015, at 11:27 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

RStan gives you treedepth, actual number of leapfrog steps (which may be less
than 2^depth due to divergences), and average acceptance probabilty for
the slice as detailed in Hoffman and Gelman and in the Stan manual.

How do you compute "expected squared jumped distance" from a chain?

I can't remember how to get the info in RStan --- it's documented somewhere
in the fit object, I think.  The values are stored in the fit object in
some parallel data structure to the draws.  

Michael and Andrew should put their heads together to negotiate minimal
vs. maximal reporting defaults.  CmdStan just includes them in the summary
output and gives them in the CSV file output, but they're not included
in RStan's print(fit).

- Bob
